children: Coinbase Global, Inc. Class A (NASDAQ:COIN) faces a mix of bullish analyst support and regulatory/legal scrutiny as Goldman Sachs lifts its price target amid product expansion into tokenized stocks and AI tools, while court and NYC Council probes and heightened volatility complicate its recovery.
: Goldman Sachs raised its price target and kept a Buy on Coinbase (COIN), citing growth in brokerage and prediction markets, renewed crypto trading activity, regulatory progress and cost discipline.
: A SDNY judge on Aug 20 let portions of a class-action vs Coinbase (COIN) and some executives proceed to discovery. Surviving claims allege hidden bankruptcy risks and downplayed SEC scrutiny.
: Coinbase (COIN) launched 1:1 tokenized U.S. stocks (e.g., NVDA, AAPL, META, GOOGL) on its Base L2, allowing eligible non‑U.S. users 24/7 trading and self‑custody via B20 tokens.
: COIN shows higher volatility than Bitcoin: ~20% vs ~8.5%, 0.61 long-term correlation with BTC. Intraday swings often amplify BTC moves; prices track trading volume and can overshoot or lag BTC.
: NYC Council opened an investigation into marketing practices and influencer promotion tied to prediction‑market products, explicitly including Coinbase Global, Inc. Class A (COIN) in its review.
: COIN tests AI tools like Coinbase Advisor. CEO Brian Armstrong says AI agents could enable real‑time micro machine-to-machine trades and urges lighter AI rules and clearer crypto regulation.
